payload.reason: The evidence provides specific metrics and methods for measuring the quality of word vectors, including the use of Pearson correlation coefficient and the impact of noise distribution on vector quality.

claims.text: The quality of word vectors is measured using the Pearson correlation coefficient between human judgment of word similarity and cosine distances in vector space.
The choice of noise distribution for negative sampling significantly affects the quality of learned word vectors, with empirical trials guiding the selection.
Improvements in word vector quality can be achieved by employing a sub-sampled unigram distribution for negative sampling.
